verses.text: Let me sing for my beloved, a song about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hill.
He dug the ground, cleared out the stones, and planted the finest vines. He built a tower in the middle and carved out a winepress. He expected good grapes, but it grew wild ones.
“Now, people of Jerusalem and Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard? When I expected grapes, why did it produce wild ones?
Now I'll tell you what I'll do to my vineyard. I'll pull out its hedge, and it'll be eaten up. I'll break down its wall, and it'll be trampled.
I'll make it a wasteland. No one will prune it or hoe it. Briers and thorns will grow, and I'll tell the clouds not to rain on it.”

The vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel. The people of Judah are the planting he delights in. He looked for justice and found oppression. He looked for righteousness and heard a cry of distress.
Trouble for those who add house to house and field to field until there's no room left and you live alone in the middle of the land!
I heard the LORD of Armies say, “Many houses will be deserted. Even the large and beautiful ones will stand empty.
Ten acres of vineyard will yield just one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will yield only an ephah.”
Trouble for those who get up early to chase strong drink and stay up late until wine sets them on fire!
They feast with harp, lyre, tambourine, flute, and wine, but they pay no attention to what the LORD does or consider the work of his hands.
So my people go into captivity for lack of knowledge. Their honored men are starving, and their crowds are parched with thirst.
So Sheol has opened its mouth wide, its appetite without limit. Their glory, their crowds, their pomp, and those celebrating among them go down into it.
People are brought low, humanity is humbled, and the eyes of the arrogant are lowered.
But the LORD of Armies is exalted through justice, and God the Holy One shows himself holy through righteousness.
Lambs will graze as in their own pasture, and strangers will eat where the rich once lived.
Trouble for those who drag wrongdoing along with cords of lies and pull wickedness like a cart on a rope.
They say, “Tell him to hurry up and do his work so we can see it. Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come close so we can know what it is!”
Trouble for those who call evil good and good evil, who pass off darkness as light and light as darkness, and who swap bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!
Trouble for those who think they're wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
Trouble for those who are heroes at drinking wine and champions at mixing strong drinks,
who take bribes to clear the guilty and deny justice to the innocent!

Just as flames consume stubble and dry grass collapses in the fire, their roots will rot and their blossoms will blow away like dust. They rejected the law of the LORD of Armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

The LORD's anger burns against his people. He's stretched out his hand against them and struck them. The mountains shake, and their bodies lie like garbage in the streets. Through all this his anger hasn't turned away. His hand is still stretched out.
He'll raise a banner to nations far away and whistle for them from the ends of the earth. Look, they'll come swift and fast.
None of them will tire or stumble. None will doze or sleep. No belt will come loose, and no sandal strap will break.
Their arrows are sharp and all their bows drawn. Their horses' hooves are like flint, and their wheels are like a whirlwind.
They'll roar like a lioness and like young lions. They'll roar, seize their prey, and carry it off, with no one to rescue it.
On that day they'll roar against the people like the sea. Look toward the land and there's darkness and distress. The clouds shut out the light.
